answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie voting weight to a refundable stake bond that vests slowly, like a cedar gaining height over seasons rather than overnight. New agents must climb a trellis of peer attestations, each rung costing real collateral and time, before their influence reaches its zenith. Spinning up clones then multiplies cost instead of power, since every fake identity needs its own vested bond and its own earned attestations.
